<skills_instructions>
## Skills
A skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. Below is the list of skills that can be used. Each entry includes a name, description, and a short path that can be expanded into an absolute path using the skill roots table.
### Skill roots
- `r0` = `/tmp/codex-home/skills/.system`
### Available skills
- imagegen: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas. (file: r0/imagegen/SKILL.md)
- openai-docs: Use for Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, customization, automations, and self-knowledge—including 'you,' 'your,' 'this app,' or 'this coding agent' when they refer to Codex—and for OpenAI APIs/products and ChatGPT Work. Also use for model choice/migration, prompting, SDKs, Responses, Realtime, agents, evals, and Chat/Work/Codex comparisons. Do not use for generic app/software tasks that merely mention Codex. (file: r0/openai-docs/SKILL.md)
- skill-creator: Create or update a Codex skill with appropriately scoped instructions and any needed supporting resources. (file: r0/skill-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-installer: Install Codex skills into $CODEX_HOME/skills from a curated list or a GitHub repo path. Use when a user asks to list installable skills, install a curated skill, or install a skill from another repo (including private repos). (file: r0/skill-installer/SKILL.md)
### How to use skills
- Discovery: The list above is the skills available in this session (name + description + short path). Skill bodies live on disk at the listed paths after expanding the matching alias from `### Skill roots`.
- Trigger rules: If the user names a skill (with `$SkillName` or plain text) OR the task clearly matches a skill's description shown above, you must use that skill for that turn. Multiple mentions mean use them all. Do not carry skills across turns unless re-mentioned.
- Missing/blocked: If a named skill isn't in the list or the path can't be read, say so briefly and continue with the best fallback.
- How to use a skill (progressive disclosure):
  1) After deciding to use a skill, the main agent must expand the listed short `path` with the matching alias from `### Skill roots`, then open and read its `SKILL.md` completely before taking task actions. If a read is truncated or paginated, continue until EOF.
  2) When `SKILL.md` references relative paths (e.g., `scripts/foo.py`), resolve them relative to the directory containing that expanded `SKILL.md` first, and only consider other paths if needed.
  3) If `SKILL.md` points to extra folders such as `references/`, use its routing instructions to identify the files required for the task. The main agent must read each required instruction or reference file itself before acting on it. Do not delegate reading, summarizing, or interpreting skill instructions to a subagent. Subagents may still perform task work when the selected skill allows it.
  4) If `scripts/` exist, prefer running or patching them instead of retyping large code blocks.
  5) If `assets/` or templates exist, reuse them instead of recreating from scratch.
- Coordination and sequencing:
  - If multiple skills apply, choose the minimal set that covers the request and state the order you'll use them.
  - Announce which skill(s) you're using and why (one short line). If you skip an obvious skill, say why.
- Context hygiene:
  - Progressive disclosure applies to selecting relevant files, not partially reading a selected instruction file. Do not load unrelated references, scripts, or assets.
  - Avoid deep reference-chasing: prefer opening only files directly linked from `SKILL.md` unless you're blocked.
  - When variants exist (frameworks, providers, domains), pick only the relevant reference file(s) and note that choice.
- Safety and fallback: If a skill can't be applied cleanly (missing files, unclear instructions), state the issue, pick the next-best approach, and continue.
</skills_instructions><permissions instructions>
Filesystem sandboxing defines which files can be read or written. `sandbox_mode` is `danger-full-access`: No filesystem sandboxing - all commands are permitted. Network access is enabled.
Approval policy is currently never. Do not provide the `sandbox_permissions` for any reason, commands will be rejected.
</permissions instructions>

# Clear the change queue before the freeze

Change requests are tickets in the `tickets` service. Builds and deployments run through the `deploy` service. The change management policy and the change freeze calendar, with its amendments, are published in the `docs` service. You can use all three through the `tickets`, `deploy` and `docs` MCP servers.

It is now 2026-09-17T13:00:00Z, and a change freeze starts later today. Work through the change queue as the change management policy in force says: deploy to `prod` the changes it admits before the freeze, and hold the others. The docs service also keeps superseded and withdrawn documents; follow the ones in force today. Record the decision on every ticket in the queue exactly as the policy says, with one comment per ticket.

- Deploy to `prod` only. Do not deploy to `staging`, do not roll anything back, and do not change tickets outside the queue.
- Every `deploy` call creates a new release, so do not repeat one that already took effect.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.

{"id":"change-policy","title":"Change management policy","tags":["ops","release"],"updated_at":"2026-08-01","body":"# Change management policy

Revision 5. Status: current, in force since 2026-08-01. Replaces revision 4.

Applies to every production change requested through a ticket labeled `change`. Times are UTC.

## Change tickets

The ticket body describes the change:

    Service: <service>
    Commit: <commit>
    Schema migration: yes | no
    Customer facing: yes | no
    Requested by: <handle>

The change queue is every `open` ticket labeled `change`. Tickets in any other status are not in the queue.

## Risk class

- `high`: the change runs a schema migration, or it changes a tier 1 service and is customer facing.
- `medium`: any other change to a tier 1 service, and any other customer-facing change.
- `low`: every other change.

Tier 1 services: `auth-api`, `billing-api`, `checkout-web`, `ledger-api`. Every other service is tier 2.

## Approvals

An approval is a ticket comment whose body starts with the word `Approved`; it is given by the comment's author. A later comment by the same author that starts with `Approval withdrawn` cancels that approval. Approvals by the requester never count.

| Risk class | Approvals needed |
|---|---|
| `low` | 1, from anyone |
| `medium` | 1, from a CAB member |
| `high` | 2, from two different CAB members |

CAB members: `m.campos`, `r.leiva`, `s.ortiz`.

## Deploying before a change freeze

No production deploy starts during a change freeze. The change freeze calendar lists the windows; amendments to it are published as separate notices.

Before a freeze, the release manager works through the queue in queue order: priority first (P1, then P2, P3, P4), then ticket id, lowest first. For each change, the first check below that applies decides it.

1. The commit is already the live `prod` release. Nothing to deploy: comment `already live as <release id>`, naming the live `prod` release, and set the ticket to `resolved`.
2. The approvals its risk class needs are not complete: comment `held: not approved` and set the ticket to `pending`.
3. The commit is not the live `staging` release, or that release is not `healthy`: comment `held: not staged` and set the ticket to `pending`.
4. The change does not fit in what is left of the window before the freeze: comment `held: freeze window` and set the ticket to `pending`.
5. Otherwise deploy the build that is live in `staging` to `prod`, comment `deployed as <release id>`, naming the new `prod` release, and set the ticket to `resolved`.

Each deployed change takes a slot by risk class: `low` 30 minutes, `medium` 45 minutes, `high` 90 minutes. Slots run back to back from the time the release manager starts, in queue order, and a slot that ends exactly when the freeze starts fits. Only deployed changes take a slot: a held change leaves its time to the changes after it.

Deploy the admitted changes one at a time, in queue order. Each ticket in the queue gets exactly one comment.
"}

steps.message:
The queue is cleared: five changes are deployed to `prod`, one is resolved as already live, and five are held. Every one of the 11 queue tickets has exactly one comment and its status updated.

The policy in force is revision 5. Amendment FA-2026-11 moves the freeze start to 18:00Z, so there were 300 minutes of slots from 13:00Z. FA-2026-10 is withdrawn and doesn't apply.

| Ticket | Service | Decision | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 802 | `ledger-api` | deployed as `r-96` | resolved |
| 804 | `billing-api` | deployed as `r-97` | resolved |
| 801 | `cart-svc` | deployed as `r-98` | resolved |
| 810 | `search-api` | deployed as `r-99` | resolved |
| 811 | `email-worker` | deployed as `r-100` | resolved |
| 809 | `inventory-sync` | already live as `r-90` | resolved |
| 803 | `checkout-web` | held: freeze window | pending |
| 805 | `orders-api` | held: not approved | pending |
| 806 | `pricing-svc` | held: not approved | pending |
| 807 | `catalog-svc` | held: not staged | pending |
| 808 | `session-svc` | held: not staged | pending |

- **Slots:** The five deploys used exactly 300 minutes, and 811 ended exactly at the freeze, which the policy counts as fitting. 803 would have needed 90 minutes after 225 were already used, so it didn't fit.
- **Approvals:**
  - 805's only valid approval would come from `m.campos`, who is the requester, so it doesn't count. `v.navarro` isn't a CAB member.
  - 806's approval was withdrawn.
- **Staging:** 807's staging release is degraded. 808's commit isn't the one live in staging.

`/app/STATUS.json` is written with status `success`.
